answer.evidence: The informative layer-1 units split into two mirrored families. Large-blob family (units 3, 7, 8, 21, 22, 24, 27, 28): strong positive weights on an annulus, roughly rows 5-18 and cols 6-18; negative weights on the very centre (rows 10-13, cols 10-13); mildly negative weights on the background. Small-blob family (units 2, 4, 14, 17, 18, 19, 25, 26, 29, 30): positive weights on the centre, negative on the annulus, positive on the background. The other units (0, 1, 5, 6, 9-13, 15, 16, 20, 23, 31) carry only small, unstructured weights of about ±25. Layer 2 combines the two families with opposite signs. For example, u1, u7, u8 and u15 read the annulus units positively and feed the output positively. u9 and u11 read the centre/background units positively and have output weights of -86 and -73. Outside the blob region I found some individual background pixels with consistently large, opposite-signed weights in the two families, such as (1,0), (1,16-17), (8,0), (8,2), (3,12), (19,2), (20,19), (16,21) and (23,7). These are isolated pixels scattered across the whole background, not a compact block. Their signs simply follow each family's general background sign, which fits per-pixel overfitting or noise rather than a coherent spurious marker. I checked every corner and edge patch and none has a uniform block of strong weights that would indicate a planted patch or marker.
answer.main_feature: The model measures blob radius with centre-versus-annulus detectors. Brightness in a ring at medium radius (about 4-8 px from the centre) drives the large-blob units and the class-1 pathway. Brightness confined to the central few pixels, with a dark ring, drives the small-blob units and the class-0 pathway.
